full_text_en:
Commercial Bank of Xi'an v. Jianqiao Securities Co., Ltd. and Western Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan guarantee contract

Ruling Summary

(1) According to Article 4 of the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, a people's court, when confirming the invalidity of a contract, shall base its decision on laws enacted by the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee and administrative regulations formulated by the State Council, and shall not base its decision on local regulations or administrative rules. The Notice of the People's Bank of China on Prohibiting Bank Funds from Illegally Flowing into the Stock Market is a departmental rule and cannot serve as the basis for confirming the validity of a contract.

(2) Where a debtor fails to repay the loan within the time limit agreed in the contract without justifiable reasons, and the guarantor fails to assume the guarantee liability as agreed in the contract, both constitute a breach of contract in the performance of the contract and should originally bear liability for breach of contract. However, if the debtor and the guarantor, on the contrary, claim the invalidity of the contract on improper grounds, this violates the principle of good faith and should not be supported by law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 150

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Commercial Bank of Xi'an, domiciled at No. 35, Dongsi Road, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Huang Lianxi, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Zhao Liming, lawyer of Shaanxi Haipu Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Qin Baogui, lawyer of Shaanxi Haipu Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Jianqiao Securities Co., Ltd., domiciled at 16th Floor and 23rd Floor, Development Bank Building, No. 2, Gaoxin First Road, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Li Xiaoyuan, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Li, lawyer of Beijing Zhonglun Wende Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Feng Jiyong, lawyer of Beijing Zhonglun Wende Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Western Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd., domiciled at 6th Floor, Zhongtian International Building, No. 3, Beidajie, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Wenbiao, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Yang Zhengtong, lawyer of Beijing Yuandong Law Firm.

The appellant, Commercial Bank of Xi'an (hereinafter referred to as Xi'an Commercial Bank), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2005) Shan Min Er Chu Zi No. 2 rendered by the High People's Court of Shaanxi Province in the case of a dispute over a loan guarantee contract with the respondents, Jianqiao Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jianqiao Securities) and Western Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Guarantee Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Judge Jiang Wei as the presiding judge, Judge Yu Songbo, and Acting Judge Yin Yuan. The court clerk was Zhang Yongshu. The case has now been concluded.

The High People's Court of Shaanxi Province found the following facts at first instance: On June 7, 2004, Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities entered into an interbank lending contract, stipulating: the lending party is Xi'an Commercial Bank (Party A), the borrowing party is Jianqiao Securities (Party B), the lending amount is RMB 36.03 million, the lending period is 7 days, i.e., from June 10, 2004, to June 17, 2004; the lending interest rate is 6.6%, and the purpose of the lending is to cover the position. The contract also stipulated: Party A's disbursement of funds and Party B's repayment of funds shall be made in accordance with the following provisions: for local transfers, the funds shall be transferred to the other party's account before 4:00 p.m. on the date of disbursement (or maturity); for cross-regional transfers, the funds shall be transferred to the other party's account via the People's Bank of China's electronic interbank system or urgent telegraphic transfer before 9:30 a.m. on the date of disbursement (or maturity), to ensure the remittance slip arrives on the same day. If the above requirements are not complied with, causing losses due to the failure of funds to arrive on time, the defaulting party shall bear the losses. Party B must repay the principal and interest of the lending in full and on time. In case of overdue payment, in addition to charging interest on the overdue amount at the agreed interest rate, a penalty interest of 0.05% per day shall be charged from the date of overdue, to be paid by Party B to Party A. Interest on the lending shall be paid along with the principal. On the same day, the Guarantee Company issued a guarantee letter to Xi'an Commercial Bank, expressing its willingness to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the repayment of the full principal and interest under the above interbank lending contract. After the contract was signed, Xi'an Commercial Bank transferred RMB 36.03 million to Jianqiao Securities by telegraphic transfer on June 10 of the same year. After the contract expired, Jianqiao Securities did not repay the loan as agreed, and the Guarantee Company also did not repay the borrowed funds to Xi'an Commercial Bank.

On November 11, 2004, after failed collection efforts, Xi'an Commercial Bank filed a lawsuit with the High People's Court of Shaanxi Province, requesting that Jianqiao Securities and the Guarantee Company repay the principal of RMB 36.03 million of the borrowed funds, as well as interest and penalty interest up to the date of payment, and bear all litigation costs of this case.

The High People's Court of Shaanxi Province held after trial: The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the interbank lending contract is valid. Relevant legal provisions provide that interbank lending is a short-term fund lending activity between banks and non-bank financial institutions. The lending between Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities is an interbank lending between a bank and a non-bank financial institution. Article 46 of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Interbank lending shall comply with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China." Paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 3 of the Notice of the People's Bank of China on Prohibiting Bank Funds from Illegally Flowing into the Stock Market issued on June 6, 1997, stipulate: "The period for securities companies to borrow funds shall not exceed 1 day, the total amount of borrowed funds shall not exceed 80% of the institution's paid-in capital, and borrowed funds can only be used for position adjustment and not for securities trading." "Any lending activity between commercial banks and non-bank financial institutions, or between non-bank financial institutions, must be conducted through the national interbank lending market (including local financing centers), and all off-market lending activities are prohibited." It can be seen that as a securities company, for the purpose of covering its position, in interbank lending business with banks, there is only a 1-day borrowing period, and the lending activity must be conducted through the national interbank lending market (including local financing centers). Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities agreed on a 7-day lending period, and the lending was not conducted through the national interbank lending market; instead, Xi'an Commercial Bank directly remitted the borrowed funds into Jianqiao Securities' account. Therefore, the interbank lending contract not only violated the above provisions of the People's Bank of China but also violated the relevant provisions of Article 17, paragraph 1, of the Measures for Punishing Financial Illegal Acts promulgated by the State Council. Consequently, the lending contract signed between Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities should be deemed invalid because its content violated the mandatory provisions of national financial laws and regulations. Both parties were at fault for the invalidity of the contract and should bear corresponding liability for fault according to law. Jianqiao Securities should return the principal of RMB 36.03 million borrowed and pay Xi'an Commercial Bank the expenses during the period of fund occupation at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period. Xi'an Commercial Bank's claim for Jianqiao Securities to pay interest and penalty interest as agreed in the contract should be dismissed according to law. Although Jianqiao Securities' defense that it does not pay the agreed interest due to the invalidity of the contract is tenable, it should still pay the expenses during the period of fund occupation. Since the principal contract is invalid, the guarantee contract is also invalid. Although the Guarantee Company does not assume joint and several guarantee liability, as a professional guarantee company, it should have known that Jianqiao Securities did not have the qualification as a member of the national interbank market and could not conduct a 7-day interbank lending business. Nevertheless, it issued the guarantee letter, expressing its willingness to assume joint and several guarantee liability for Jianqiao Securities' lending activity. Therefore, it is at fault for the invalidity of the guarantee contract and should bear corresponding civil liability according to law, i.e., it shall bear joint and several compensation liability for one-third of the part of Jianqiao Securities' above debt that cannot be recovered. The Guarantee Company's defense that it does not bear guarantee liability due to the invalidity of the contract is tenable, but its compensation liability cannot be exempted according to law. The Guarantee Company's defense that the Guarantee Letter was only an expression of guarantee intention, no formal Guarantee Contract was signed, and there was no board resolution, so the guarantee act should be invalid, is a misunderstanding of the guarantee contract and cannot be established. The Guarantee Company's defense that Xi'an Commercial Bank failed to exercise its rights against the guarantor within the statutory guarantee period, and that the case was filed on November 11, 2004, and fees were paid on November 23, 2004, without an application for deferral from Xi'an Commercial Bank, should be deemed as automatic withdrawal of the lawsuit, is inconsistent with the objective facts and cannot be established. According to Article 52, paragraph 1, item (5) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 5 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 8 and 9 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled as follows: (1) The interbank lending contract between Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities, and the guarantee letter issued by the Guarantee Company to Xi'an Commercial Bank, are invalid; (2) Jianqiao Securities shall return the principal of RMB 36.03 million to Xi'an Commercial Bank within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, and shall pay the fund occupation fee at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period (from June 10, 2004, to the date the judgment takes effect). For overdue performance, execution shall be carried out in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; (3) The Guarantee Company shall bear joint and several compensation liability for one-third of the part of Jianqiao Securities' above debt that cannot be satisfied; (4) After the Guarantee Company bears compensation liability to Xi'an Commercial Bank, it may recover from Jianqiao Securities within the scope of the compensation liability; (5) Dismiss Xi'an Commercial Bank's other claims. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 190,160 shall be borne by Jianqiao Securities.

Dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the original trial court, Xi'an Commercial Bank appealed to this Court, arguing: The original judgment clearly erred in the application of law and was improper in its decision. (1) The Notice on Prohibiting Bank Funds from Illegally Flowing into the Stock Market has become invalid. On December 17, 2004, the People's Bank of China and the China Banking Regulatory Commission issued the Announcement on the Results of the First Batch of 110 Rules and Regulatory Documents (Announcement No. 20 of 2004), which explicitly abolished the said notice. The original judgment, five months after the notice was abolished, still used it as the basis for determining the invalidity of the contract in this case, which is a clear error in the application of law. (2) The interbank lending contract signed between Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities did not violate the Measures for Punishing Financial Illegal Acts, and the interbank lending contract and guarantee contract in this case are valid and legal. Neither laws nor administrative regulations have clearly stipulated the specific conditions for interbank lending. The State Council's Measures for Punishing Financial Illegal Acts also does not specify the conditions, qualifications, or periods for interbank lending; it only imposes penalties for financial illegal acts that violate the provisions of the People's Bank of China. Article 9 of the People's Bank of China's Administrative Provisions on Securities Companies Entering the Interbank Market stipulates: "Securities companies that have been approved as members of the national interbank market must conduct interbank lending and bond trading through the trading system provided by the National Interbank Funding Center." Article 13 stipulates: "Securities companies that have not become members of the national interbank market shall still conduct one-day interbank lending business through their headquarters according to the original provisions." Based on these provisions, Xi'an Commercial Bank's lending of funds to Jianqiao Securities, which had interbank lending qualifications, should be a lawful act. The contract signed by both parties is valid and legal. Even if the lending exceeded the prescribed period, it would not lead to the invalidity of the lending contract, nor should it deprive the lender of protection for the interest and penalty interest on overdue repayment agreed in the contract. (3) The original judgment was improper. The interbank lending contract in this case is common in practice and is a prevailing market practice. If such interbank lending contracts are deemed invalid, normal financial business will be difficult to conduct, and the legitimate rights and interests of banks will be left unprotected. More importantly, no laws or regulations have prohibited this type of interbank lending business. The original judgment, without considering the true intentions of the parties to the contract and the specific circumstances of the contract having been performed, declared the interbank lending contract and guarantee contract invalid, which is indeed improper. Xi'an Commercial Bank requested the revocation of the original judgment and a judgment ordering Jianqiao Securities to repay the borrowed principal and interest and penalty interest as agreed in the contract, with the Guarantee Company assuming joint and several guarantee liability for this debt.

The respondent Jianqiao Securities argued in its defense: (1) The announcement on December 17, 2004, by the People's Bank of China and the China Banking Regulatory Commission (CBRC) on the results of the first batch of rules and regulatory documents did not explicitly abolish the Notice on Prohibiting Bank Funds from Illegally Flowing into the Stock Market. Instead, it clarified that the regulatory document would be supervised, implemented, explained, amended, and abolished by the People's Bank of China and the CBRC according to their respective statutory functions. Therefore, the notice has not become invalid. Even if the notice has now become invalid, the lending activity in this case occurred on June 7, 2004, a time when the regulatory document was still effective. The first-instance court applied the provisions that were effective at that time, which was not improper. (2) Xi'an Commercial Bank's understanding of the Measures for Punishing Financial Illegal Acts is erroneous. According to the Administrative Provisions on Securities Companies Entering the Interbank Market and the Measures for Punishing Financial Illegal Acts, the interbank lending contract in this case exceeded the prescribed period and was not conducted through the national interbank lending market, violating the mandatory provisions of national financial regulations and therefore is an invalid contract. The first-instance court correctly applied the law. (3) Xi'an Commercial Bank's argument that the interbank lending contract in this case is a common market practice lacks factual basis. Its claim was not properly supported by evidence within the statutory period for submission and is clearly a violation of the law. This ground of appeal cannot be established. The respondent requested the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

The respondent Guarantee Company argued in its defense: (1) The Notice on Prohibiting Bank Funds from Illegally Flowing into the Stock Market, which the first-instance judgment relied on, has not become invalid. It only redefined the subject that exercises the power of supervision, implementation, interpretation, amendment, and abolition. Even if Xi'an Commercial Bank's understanding of the People's Bank of China's announcement is correct, according to the principle that laws have no retroactive effect, the first-instance court's application of the regulation was correct. (2) The State Council's Measures for Punishing Financial Illegal Acts was formulated to penalize acts that violate national financial laws and regulations. The premise for imposing penalties is that financial institutions have violated the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China and other departments. Therefore, acts that violate the People's Bank of China's maximum lending period are naturally included. Moreover, Article 17 of the Measures expressly prohibits acts that exceed the maximum lending period. Therefore, lending activities that exceed the maximum lending period stipulated by the People's Bank of China also violate the mandatory provisions of the Measures, and the judgment that the principal contract in this case is invalid based on the Measures is correct. The respondent requested the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

Upon second-instance trial, this Court confirms the facts found by the original trial court.

This Court holds: The focus of the dispute in the second instance among Xi'an Commercial Bank, Jianqiao Securities, and the Guarantee Company is still the validity of the interbank lending contract and the guarantee contract. The main reasons for the original trial court to find the interbank lending contract invalid were, first, that the term of the interbank lending contract signed between Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities exceeded the period stipulated by the People's Bank of China, and second, that the lending activity was not conducted through the national interbank lending market. The original trial court's reasons were based on the provisions of the People's Bank of China's Notice on Prohibiting Bank Funds from Illegally Flowing into the Stock Market and the State Council's Measures for Punishing Financial Illegal Acts. The People's Bank of China's Notice on Prohibiting Bank Funds from Illegally Flowing into the Stock Market is a departmental rule in terms of its rank in the hierarchy of normative documents. According to Article 4 of this Court's Interpretation (I) on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China: "After the implementation of the Contract Law, a people's court, when confirming the invalidity of a contract, shall base its decision on laws enacted by the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee and administrative regulations formulated by the State Council, and shall not base its decision on local regulations or administrative rules." Therefore, the Notice, as an administrative rule, cannot serve as the basis for confirming the invalidity of a contract. The State Council's Measures for Punishing Financial Illegal Acts concerns how administrative penalties should be imposed on financial institutions that violate relevant national financial management provisions. Article 17 of the Measures stipulates that if a financial institution engages in lending activities with acts such as exceeding the maximum lending period or conducting interbank lending outside the national unified interbank lending network, it shall be subject to penalties such as suspension or cessation of the business and confiscation of illegal gains. It can be seen that this provision has nothing to do with the validity of the contract. Therefore, the validity of the interbank lending contract cannot be determined based on the provisions of the Measures. The original trial court's finding that the interbank lending contract signed between Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities violated the mandatory provisions of national financial laws and regulations and was invalid is erroneous and should be corrected.

After Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities signed the interbank lending contract, Jianqiao Securities used the borrowed funds for the agreed purpose of covering its position. There was no act of using bank funds for securities trading. Therefore, the lending activity between Xi'an Commercial Bank and Jianqiao Securities was the true expression of the intentions of both parties, did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and did not harm national interests or public social interests. The interbank lending contract between the parties should be deemed valid. The Guarantee Company issued a guarantee letter, clearly expressing its willingness to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the above interbank lending contract. Since the principal contract is valid and there are no other circumstances rendering the guarantee contract invalid, the guarantee liability of the Guarantee Company should not be exempted. After the contract was actually performed, i.e., after receiving the urgently needed funds, Jianqiao Securities, as the repayment obligor, failed to repay the loan within the agreed period without justifiable reasons, and the Guarantee Company failed to assume joint and several guarantee liability as agreed. Both constituted a breach of contract in the performance of the contract and should originally bear liability for breach of contract. However, Jianqiao Securities and the Guarantee Company, on the contrary, argued that the contract was invalid on grounds such as the lending exceeding the statutory period. This argument is legally unfounded and violates the principle of good faith; it should not be supported.

In summary, Xi'an Commercial Bank's grounds of appeal are valid and are supported by this Court. The original judgment found the facts clearly but erred in the application of law and should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court judges as follows:

1. Revoke the civil judgment (2005) Shan Min Er Chu Zi No. 2 of the High People's Court of Shaanxi Province;
2. Jianqiao Securities Co., Ltd. shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, repay to Commercial Bank of Xi'an the principal of RMB 36.03 million and interest, with overdue penalty interest to be calculated and paid in installments according to the then-current overdue penalty interest calculation standards of the People's Bank of China;
3. Western Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several liability for the discharge of the above debt of Jianqiao Securities Co., Ltd.;
4. After Western Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd. has borne the guarantee liability to Commercial Bank of Xi'an, it has the right to recover from Jianqiao Securities Co., Ltd.

The first-instance and second-instance case acceptance fees are each RMB 190,160, to be borne by Jianqiao Securities Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jiang Wei
Judge: Yu Songbo
Acting Judge: Yin Yuan

September 27, 2005

Court Clerk: Zhang Yongshu
